  Compilers choose better implementations only from transformations a

  are transported through an evidence store, derivability is credited

# Introduction

Every optimization a production compiler knows was written by a
person — a hand-derived rule, encoded per framework.  The rule
library is the bottleneck: human authorship is slow, and the
pairings nobody names never get found.  For a machine to *author*
optimizations, four things must exist: rules it can write (data, not
code), a referee to check them, a score to rank them, and a world —
a runtime — that programs, rules, and derivations all live inside.

The pieces have arrived separately.  Massalin's superoptimizer
[@massalin1987superoptimizer] searched programs exhaustively;
equality saturation [@tate2009; @willsey2021egg] closes the program
space under a fixed law bank, and TENSAT applies it to tensor
graphs.  Rule-inference work (Ruler [@nandi2021ruler], the Babble
line [@cao2023babble]) grows the library itself.  And learned play
on well-defined games — AlphaGo Zero [@silver2017alphago],
AlphaTensor [@fawzi2022alphatensor] — reaches structure beyond
human-written heuristics.  The synthesis story for *tensor
programs with runtime-priced deployment*, though, is thinner: no
system connects discovery, certification, pricing, shipping, and
learned guidance inside one substrate.

This paper reports the connection — and one complete measured traversal
of it — in the mlopt engine.  The contribution is not any single
mechanism but their composition: a categorical substrate makes rules
data, derivations checkable, cost measurable, and provides the runtime
world — which closes discovery into a well-defined game played by
learned policies.  The enabling property is *self-containedness*:
programs, rewrite laws, and derivations are n-morphisms in one calculus —
executable values, not external metadata — so the system produces the
values it consumes.  To our knowledge this is the first *operational*
substrate of this kind; categorical languages prior to it are
denotational or design-level, not working machines whose runtime
executes the morphism hierarchy.  The claim is narrow and checkable:

> A rewrite a hand optimizer would write — the eval-mode conv+BN
> weight fold — was **discovered, certified, priced, and shipped by the
> machine**, and its deployed form runs bitwise-equal and cheaper
> through an independent runtime.

No model-scale speedup is claimed.  The result is kernel-scale
(one op pair, fp64 fixtures), the runtime is a tree-walk interpreter
(debug build), and the move alphabet is bounded by the 28-op
host-tensor surface — all named in @sec-limitations.  What the case study
establishes is the *pipeline*: that a law can travel from measured
need to a shipped, certified, runtime-priced rule without a human
writing it.

The repository is `handl-lang/graphopt`; every number below
cites the artifact that produced it (§@sec-repro).

# Background {#sec-background}

## Equality saturation

An e-graph compactly represents the closure of a term under a law
bank — all reachable spellings, sharing subterms, to a fixed point
[@tate2009] — and extraction picks the cheapest member under a cost
model.  The machinery lives in `handl-lang/eqsat` and the platform
paper [@eqsat2026substrate] describes it once: the term IR, the
bounded saturation, the certificate and cost algebra.  This paper
recounts only what the discovery story uses.  One piece does carry
over verbatim: the soundness boundary is the law bank — a rule's
side conditions are the *only* layer that keeps a false member out,
and the certificate replay re-proves that a step is a valid
application, not that the rule is true.

## Laws as data on a categorical substrate

Catopt reads a program as a 1-morphism between tensor types, a rewrite
law as a 2-cell between programs, and a derivation — one law proven
from premises — as a 3-cell: the cells-as-data pattern the kernel
calculus defines [@kernel2026] and the eqsat paper operationalises
[@eqsat2026substrate].  The consequence is that laws
are **data rows** (a pattern pair plus a `cond`/`check`/`derive`
guard spec), serializable, storable, composable — and what this paper
mutates is the bank: `mlopt_core.laws.ALL_RULES` mixes human-authored
axioms with thirteen machine-admitted objects
(`mlopt_core.laws.provenance.MACHINE_SHIPPED`).

## The handl substrate and mlopt-kit

The same "one language, many interpretations" model is implemented by
the handl platform — the closed arrow calculus and `Language` schema
are the kernel paper's subject [@kernel2026]: eval, typecheck and
rewrite are interpretations of one language whose tables are data.
`packages/mlopt-kit` — a plain
Rust crate — composes handl's canonical `Language`, its
lex/parse/tree-walk-exec engines, and `handl-host-tensor`'s 28-op
`tensor.*` surface as dependencies (no forks).  `hnl-run` is a
subprocess door: `.hnl` in, a JSON wire tensor out, `--repeat N`
evaluating a source N times in one process — the measurement hook.
`bench/drivers/kit/term_hnl.py` renders any mlopt IR term as a `.hnl` program
from a data table (per-op arg assembly, attr marshaling, leaf binding),
so the *same object the e-graph rewrites* is what the runtime
executes.

# Machinery {#sec-machinery}

## The mint fixpoint

`mlopt_core.meta.synthesize_rules` runs the substrate's bounded mint
fixpoint [@eqsat2026substrate] over the law bank on a seed term —
apply the rules, compose the pairs that chain, emit `syn_*`
composites carrying premise provenance.  On the eval-mode
ConvBN seed it emits 974 rules in $\approx$ 12 s (fuel 30,000, 4 rounds);
the fold composite mints deterministically (identical names across
runs).

## Guard transport

A minted rule's side conditions are closures over its premise objects,
so the evidence store keeps them as *specs*, not code — parent names
plus re-expression maps — and `evidence.admit_object` rebuilds
`check`/`derive` by resolving parents transitively; the substrate's
shipped form (`mlopt_core.laws.minted`) embeds the records and
replays the rebuild at import, refusing a degraded parent
[@eqsat2026substrate].

## Premise-anchored derivability

`verify_law` answers "is this instance derivable under a rule bank?"
with a replayable witness, and for a stored composite the honest
question — derivability under the premises it was minted from — is
the substrate's anti-gaming discipline [@eqsat2026substrate]: the
certificate must be standalone-replayable and every step naming a
non-axiom rule must *site-verify* under the fp64 numeric oracle.  A
premise false at its applied site revokes the credit and the verdict
falls back to the axioms-only answer.

## One cost alphabet

The substrate's cost model credits compile-time work structurally
[@eqsat2026substrate]: a subtree closed over `Param`/`Const` leaves
whose root op is in `FOLD_OPS` — the 161-op fold-at-lowering
alphabet — is priced at ~0 marginal.  This is what lets a fold's
pay leg measure what it should: the fold's
`mul`/`reshape`/`rsqrt` chain is once-per-deployment work, not
per-call work, and `dag_cost` prices it that way.

## The admission gauntlet

`evidence.run_gauntlet` is the domain-side staging of the substrate's
admission protocol [@eqsat2026substrate]: reconstruct → full-data →
measure → truth → novelty → typed-pay → closure → certificate, with
truth the two-legged numeric-oracle-plus-derivability check and
novelty refusing re-spellings of shipped laws
(`relation=duplicate`).  What this paper adds is the record of it
biting: the gauntlet has repeatedly falsified the engine's own
candidates — a naive broadcast guard with 212 bad accepts, an
apparent paying sibling with semantically unequal sites, four
deliberate false twins (`project/retros/mul-unsq-nat.md`,
`layer3-loop.md`, `typed-pay-gate.md`).

## Learned guidance as a game {#sec-game}

Because laws are data, discovery admits a well-defined game structure
— moves are rule applications, the admission gauntlet is the
referee, the cost alphabet is the score [@eqsat2026substrate].  This
is implemented machinery, not aspiration, and it lives in
`handl-lang/gamekit`: `gamekit.engine` defines the `Board` protocol
and the episode/train/eval drivers, and `gamekit.players` provides
the `LinearPolicy` arm over a domain-specified featurizer —
`mlopt_discovery.engine`/`players` are compatibility re-export shims
over those modules.  `mlopt_discovery.play` carries the domain
registry (`meta`, `joint`, `torch`, `search`, `gen`, `open`,
`player`; `torch` and `gen` ship `deliver` hooks that lower the
winning extraction to a verified module).  A domain is data — a case
generator, a board factory, and a feature schema — not a subclass.

Two linear priors ship with pinned held-out wins: the open-game policy
ranks law candidates at ~4.7× the cost-delta heuristic's average
precision (AP 0.210 vs 0.045) and ~2× useful laws per episode, and the
meta-arena prior beats the scripted playbook (mean episode reward
−0.06 vs −0.10) — the latter flagged by its own eval as possibly
sampling-variance-riding, an honest negative kept in the record.  A
distilled contraction policy (`PairPolicyNet`) beats `opt_einsum`'s
randomized greedy (0.91× cost at n=40) and ships as a standalone
artifact.  The neural arm's residual gap is ordering credit, not
coverage: a pairwise RankNet objective on the reward's own label
reaches AP 0.1941 — above the trained-linear anchor (0.128), under
the page-aware linear (0.210) — and a ListNet-graded drain earns
heuristic-parity episode reward (0.3549 vs 0.3595, inside seed
noise) without beating it (`docs/results_neural_rank.md`).  Two
learned-policy axes were measured and falsified: learned *schedule
guidance* over the generator arms (`project/retros/guide-real-run.md`,
`guide-learned-corpus.md` — the optimal schedule reduces to a rule),
and *direct law invention* by a learned policy (~10× worse than
structured construction; ADR 0004).  The evidence for
learned guidance is real but early (controlled baseline and ablations in
`docs/results_learned_baseline.md` / `docs/results_learned_ablations.md`;
dedicated RL arms in `docs/results_learned_rl.md`): linear and distilled arms beat
baselines; neural methods reach parity, not wins.

# Case study: the conv+BN fold {#sec-casestudy}

The rewrite is the standard eval-mode fold:

$$
\mathrm{BN}_{\gamma,\beta,\mu,\sigma^2,\varepsilon}\big(\mathrm{conv}(x,W,b)\big)
\;=\; \mathrm{conv}\big(x,\; W \odot \hat{s}',\; b\odot s + (\beta - s\odot\mu)\big),
\qquad s = \gamma\cdot(\sigma^2+\varepsilon)^{-1/2}.
$$

The account below is the probe's own output
(`bench/drivers/probes/conv_fold_premise_pay_probe.py`, ~13 s).

**Anchor.**  `CONV_FOLD_RULES` provides the channel-scale and
channel-shift anchors (`mul(conv2d(x,W,b),ŝ)`-shaped single-step
folds); `BATCH_NORM_RULES` expands `batch_norm` into its affine
spelling.  Individually they are enabled-but-opt-in — the anchors
refuse at truth-starvation, the expand at typed-pay — their value is
*enablement*: they are the fold's derivation premises.

**Mint.**  `synthesize_rules` over the bank minus the already-shipped
composite emits 974 rules; the fold composite —
`batch_norm(conv2d(·),…)` → `conv2d(·)` — mints as a depth-4
`syn_*` chain over an 8-rule transitive premise closure (the
`batch_norm_expand` expansion + four `conv_channel_*` anchors +
three `syn_*` intermediates).

**Transport and truth.**  Stored with its closure, `admit_object`
rebuilds both hooks from guard records (`missing=('check','derive')`
→ transported).  The transported guard accepts the real site
(1 eq / 0 ne) and 105/105 of the guarded synth region with 255 honest
declines; `verify_law` replays the derivation under shipped axioms in
one step — `witness=('conv_bn_fold',)`, the library law proving its
own minted origin.

**Pay.**  On the 8×8 probe site the folded instance drops `dag_cost`
**34,874.3 → 17,438.7** (−50 %), fires once, verifies `pass` on the
lowered modules.

**Ship.**  The composite is promoted *verbatim*: its stored records
embed in `mlopt_core.laws.minted`, its guard re-materializes at
import, `MACHINE_SHIPPED` grows to 12 (13 today — `add_unsq_pad_r`
followed).  Re-running the gauntlet
post-ship refuses at novelty with `relation=duplicate` — the
documented signature of "already admitted."

**Runtime-verified.**  Through the kit bridge (@sec-background), the
spelled term `batch_norm(conv2d(x,W,b),…)` and the deployed term
`conv2d(x,W2,b2)` — with `W2`,`b2` themselves mlopt subterms
materialized through the kit — evaluate to the same tensor
(**bitwise-equal** on the seeded fixture; the full `torch.export` IR
of the module evaluates at 6.7e-16 max abs diff), and per-call wall
over `hnl-run --repeat 30` measures three regimes — the honest
deployed arm (fold math amortized to load) is ~−5 %; an inline-fold
arm that recomputes the fold per call runs *slower* (+22–33 %); and a
subprocess-arm −16 % figure conflates the prelude's unused fold-marshal
work into the baseline.  `dag_cost` is the stable headline:
55,296 → 36,864 (−33 %).  Full reconciliation:
`bench/RESULTS.md` + `bench/drivers/probes/conv_fold_wall_regimes_probe.py`.

: The fold decision, priced by the runtime itself — honest regime-split.
{#tbl-decision}

One honest subtlety: `dag_cost`'s param-only discount models
compile-time folding the tree-walk runtime does not perform, so the
measured arm separates fold-once (materialize `W2`,`b2`) from
run-every-call (the deployed conv).  The cost model and the wall
agree in direction; the wall numbers are debug-build timings —
directional, not a benchmark rig.

# Related work {#sec-related}

**Equality saturation and e-graph superoptimization.**  Tate et
al. [@tate2009] introduced the technique; egg [@willsey2021egg] made
it practical; TENSAT [@yang2021tensat] and follow-ons apply it to
tensor graphs with fixed, hand-written rule sets.  Catopt uses the
same substrate but the rule bank is not fixed — the discovery loop
writes into it through the gauntlet.  egglog [@zhang2023egglog]
serves as a test-only differential oracle for the hand-rolled
saturation.

**Rewrite-rule inference and library learning.**  Ruler
[@nandi2021ruler] infers rewrite rules for scalar domains by
enumeration + equality-saturation filtering — the direct ancestor of
the mint-then-verify shape here, differing in that mlopt mints
*composites over tensor laws* with transported guards and credits
derivability against an object's own premise closure.  Babble
[@cao2023babble] learns library abstractions by anti-unification;
mlopt's definitional-atom layer is the same move and measured
**null** on reach-expansion — the paying layer is above it.

**Generated rule banks.**  TASO [@jia2019taso] auto-generates graph
substitutions for DNNs and verifies them formally with an automated
theorem prover — the strongest prior on the verify-what-you-mint leg;
the generated bank ships once and does not re-enter subsequent
discovery.  Isaria [@thomas2024isaria] synthesizes *sound*
rewrite-rule systems from ISA specifications to drive e-graph
vectorizing compilers, and Enumo [@pal2023enumo] makes rule inference
programmable — both grow the bank offline, and the ruleset a compiler
runs is static.  Glenside [@smith2021glenside] is the closest
precedent for machine-derived tensor transformations: e-graphs
rediscovering access-pattern rewrites (im2col-style) — the shape of
the conv+BN fold here.

**Learned play over rewriting.**  CompilerGym
[@cummins2022compilergym] casts compiler optimization as an RL
environment over a fixed action space; the Cambridge line — Omelette
[@singh2022omelette], MCTS-GEB [@he2023mctsgeb], Aurora
[@barbulescu2024aurora] — trains RL/MCTS policies that steer e-graph
construction.  Learned play over rewriting exists, but over a static
bank.  AlphaGeometry [@trinh2024alphageometry] couples a learned
proposer to a certifying symbolic deducer — learned play inside a
verified loop, over a fixed deduction closure (AlphaTensor
[@fawzi2022alphatensor] similarly searches one fixed structure).

Each neighbor holds pieces of the loop — generation, certification,
learned play — but, to our knowledge, none makes the minted bank
itself an object of play: in mlopt a law minted during discovery
re-enters as a move inside the learned game (@sec-game).  The
differentiation is that closure, not any single leg.

Three capabilities fall out of the closure and belong to no single
neighbor.  *Two-engine certification*: a certified law must execute
identically through mlopt's e-graph *and* through handl's
independently-implemented rewrite engine (`packages/mlopt-handl-peer`;
the audit driver `bench/drivers/audit/handl_differential.py` fires the
structural bank on both and reports disagreement) — a wrong law must
fool both.  *Laws as first-class values*: minting constructs a
`Value` in the same calculus the engine executes — a data row, not
generated code — so admission is a runtime decision, not a build
step.  *Language-agnostic exits*: the `Sink` port lowers one extracted
graph to torch (`mlopt_torch.TorchSink`) or ONNX
(`mlopt_onnx.OnnxSink`), and a separate bench driver
(`bench/drivers/kit/term_hnl.py`) renders the same term as handl
`.hnl` — so a certified result is not
married to the backend that priced it.

**Compilers.**  TVM [@chen2018tvm] autotunes schedules; TorchInductor
[@ansel2024pytorch2] fuses pointwise ops and codegen's the graph a
human optimizer could reach.  Both are incumbents in the repo's
benchmark tables (wins and losses alike); the contribution here is not
a faster kernel but a certified, machine-discovered *rewrite*.

**Certified/verified compilation.**  The per-artifact boundary design —
law, search, delivery, bound each with its own verifier — is in the
spirit of translation validation; what is unusual is that the verifier
also audits the *discovery* machinery (adversarial sweeps falsifying
minted guards).

# Limitations {#sec-limitations}

- **Kernel scale.**  One op pair, fp64 fixtures, a 1×4×24×24
  activation.  Nothing here measures model-scale compilation;
  wider-corpus evidence in the repo (bimodal exposure, ~1.5% yield of
  fresh paying structure) is honest that this is not yet a general
  speedup.
- **Move alphabet bound.**  The kit surface is 28 `tensor.*` ops (16
  forwards + 11 `*_backward` adjoints + `derive`); the
  fold's own $s = \gamma \cdot \mathrm{rsqrt}(\sigma^2 + \varepsilon)$ is outside it (no elementwise
  `rsqrt`) and rides a marshaling channel.  Emitted terms are confined
  to what the surface spells; outside-surface ops refuse by name.
- **Tree-walk runtime.**  `hnl-run --repeat` timings are wall-clock on
  a debug-build tree-walk interpreter — they establish direction (the
  fold's value lands in the deployed program), not competitive
  throughput.  No codegen claim is made.
- **Single-case gauntlet.**  The admission measured here is a
  one-term corpus; the machinery's broader soundness evidence lives in
  the library-level sweeps, which caught real holes — but on
  different objects than this one.
- **Attr-narrow LHS.**  The shipped composite's LHS carries the seed's
  literal attrs (`stride=(1,1)`, `padding=(1,1)`, `eps=1e-05`,
  `training=False`): its region is the default-attr eval-mode fold —
  honest, narrow, the common spelling.
- **Novelty is closed-world.**  "Novel" in this draft means
  *machine-original against catalogued knowledge* — the decidable
  cert $\wedge$ beat $\wedge$ $\neg$derivable predicate the platform paper defines
  [@eqsat2026substrate], evaluated against `known_bank()` — the
  shipped rules plus the `prior_art` preset's `FUSION`/`CATEGORICAL`
  rows (the slice the bounded prover can saturate against) — minus
  alpha-siblings.
  The sieve (`bench/drivers/screen/novelty_sieve.py`, results in
  `docs/results_novelty_sieve.md`) ran 24 candidates: two in the
  review queue (`mul_unsq_nat`, `softsign_fold`), four derivable,
  six unpaid, twelve unmeasured.  "Novel to humanity" remains an
  open-world literature claim this draft does not make.

# Reproduction {#sec-repro}

Reproducibility is org-scoped, stated honestly.  The flagship
artifacts — the `conv_bn_fold` shipped law, `MACHINE_SHIPPED`
provenance, the `dag_cost` alphabet — live in `mlopt_core` in
`handl-lang/eqsat`, and the game layer in `handl-lang/gamekit`; both
resolve as private `git+ssh` dependencies pinned in `uv.lock`
(eqsat `b0cb5cd…`, gamekit `97c1faa…`).  The measured retros each
claim cites live under `project/retros/`, which is gitignored on
`main` — they are committed on the repo's `project` branch, not in a
`main` clone.  So: reproducible across the
`handl-lang/{graphopt,eqsat,gamekit}` trees at the locked revisions,
requiring org access — not from this repo alone.

Within that scope:

```sh
uv sync
.venv/bin/python bench/drivers/probes/conv_fold_premise_pay_probe.py   # the admission account (~13 s)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_kit_bridge.py -q       # the runtime-priced decision (8 tests)
cargo test -p mlopt-kit                                     # the Rust consumer (31 tests)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m "not slow"                     # the dev lane
```

The evidence ledger is `bench/RESULTS.md`; the measured retros each
claim cites are under `project/retros/` on the `project` branch
(notably `minted-composite-default.md`, `kit-term-bridge.md`,
`premise-anchored-derivability.md`, `fold-cost-single-source.md`);
the extended working draft with the full win/loss tables is
`docs/paper_draft.md`.
